Here's what I've learned about change, mostly the hard way. It doesn't arrive as a decision. It arrives as a pile of small refusals. I stop saying yes to the thing that drains me. Then I stop apologizing for it. Then, one day, I notice I'm not the same person who used to say yes. Is that growth? I think so. It doesn't feel heroic. It feels like housekeeping — sweeping the same floor until the floor is finally clean.
